summary: To find the projection of unit vector $\mathbf{a}$ onto the plane spanned by unit vectors $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$, we express the projection as $\mathbf{p} = p\mathbf{b} + q\mathbf{c}$. Since $\mathbf{p}$ is the orthogonal projection, the error vector $\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{p}$ must be orthogonal to both $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$. This yields the system of equations: $(\mathbf{a} - p\mathbf{b} - q\mathbf{c}) \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0$ and $(\mathbf{a} - p\mathbf{b} - q\mathbf{c}) \cdot \mathbf{c} = 0$. Given $|\mathbf{a}|=|\mathbf{b}|=|\mathbf{c}|=1$, $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=1/5$, $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{c}=1/6$, and $\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}=\cos(60^\circ)=1/2$, the system becomes $p + q/2 = 1/5$ and $p/2 + q = 1/6$. Solving this linear system yields $p = 1/10$ and $q = 1/15$. The ordered pair is $(1/10, 1/15)$.
evidence: The projection $\mathbf{p} = p\mathbf{b} + q\mathbf{c}$ satisfies $(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{b}=0 \implies \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = p(\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{b}) + q(\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{b}) \implies 1/5 = p + q/2$.

The projection $\mathbf{p} = p\mathbf{b} + q\mathbf{c}$ satisfies $(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{c}=0 \implies \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{c} = p(\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}) + q(\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{c}) \implies 1/6 = p/2 + q$.
